content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "Lemma 1's stated general form rests on a false 'infinite sunflower' fact whose inductive proof need not terminate; only the bounded-size case (used later) is genuinely provable, and the write-up doesn't restrict to it.", "errors": [{"description": "The quoted sunflower fact is false for families of unbounded set size (e.g. a nested/antichain family X_n = {1,...,n} ∪ {n'} has no infinite Δ-system), and the sketched induction ('delete that element, and continue') has no termination argument. Hence Lemma 1 as stated is unproved (and, if true, would trivialize the problem). Only the 'in particular' bounded-size case is actually applied, and there the same induction works once one restricts to sets of size ≤ K — a one-line repair.", "quote": "We use the following elementary infinite sunflower fact: every infinite family of distinct finite sets has an infinite subfamily $X_{i_1},X_{i_2},\\ldots$ for which there is a fixed set $R$ satisfying"}], "notes": "Reduction to supports, self-duality (1)-(2), the weight-descent Lemma 2, the bound 2^{|D|-1} < a_1 on terminal supports, and the final counting argument giving a_{n+T}=a_n+L are all correct and carefully done. Only the sunflower lemma statement is defective."}
